reason: The outer can-question is accurate, but the graph treats “what I described” as an embedded question. It denotes the thing to draw, with “what” also serving as the object of “described.”
The imperative takes Board minutes as its object and links the full quoted replacement text through “with.”

The coordinated imperatives connect the nodes in a star and keep the hub in the middle.
The graph treats “exits” as a noun inside the woman's clothing phrase, leaving the boy's departure as a fragment. The girl's arrival and its endpoint are represented.

The bird fragment places a tiny, left-facing bird on the fence. The next clause puts the boat on the lake, preserves “should,” and makes the tent what the boat should face, with the drawing's current appearance attached.
The graph attaches “by region” to “gridlines,” splitting the chart name “Revenue by region.”
The graph coordinates the palette imperative with the nonfinite breakdown clause inside the revenue modifier. The source coordinates the two main imperatives, “Show” and “use.”

Preserves all three commands in order, both one-row movements and their directions, and both blocks in the swap.
Captures the proposal for us to replace Postcard Ben with the quoted text and the follow-up that this would help.

Keeps the greeting and the command to leave the words on the top half of the page.

Captures the command to put a nest below the tree, with “there” retained as a location cue.

Captures “trash” as an imperative with contextual “this” as its direct object.
Makes “the” the object of “set” and attaches “from y” to the verb. The object is the “from y” property of all the arrows, and 40 is its new value.
Treats 2026 as a quantity in the hexagon label, where it is part of the name “Expenses 2026.” Both commands and the Survey results endpoint are present.

The speaker needs the addressee to sketch a car called Pine Tree, then directs placement of Pine Tree below snow. The final appreciation is also represented.
The circuit captures the dislike of the short cut on her, but treats the second “her” as a possessive determiner of “hair.” In the imperative, “her” is the recipient of the long hair.
The cat is the object of “bring,” and “up” together with “in size” expresses an increase in the cat’s size.
The graph preserves “this” as the object of “rounding off” and links the vials through “with,” but marks the standalone nonfinite clause as declarative.

The circuit captures the claims by type, visible figures, grand total, and blue bars, but groups normalization and the color directive as adverbial dependents of “need.” This misplaces the normalization qualifier and the bar-color directive.
The circuit treats “look” as a noun compounded with “woods.” It is the predicate of the action the bear is being made to perform, with the pond as the target of its gaze.
The circuit treats “book” as a noun compound in a fragment. It is the imperative predicate, with “Room 1” as its object.
The fragment supports a greeting addressed to “oval Goal,” with both words preserved in the nominal topic.
The circuit captures Review, the date, the UTC start time, and the duration, but assigns 6 as a calendar quantity. The numeral is part of the calendar identifier “Work 6.”
The fragment identifies a girl with a sad face and links her to “looking,” with “right over on the left” read as an emphatic locative phrase.
The couple of bubbles is linked to the modifier, but the first “one” is assigned as the direct object of “linked,” splitting the manner phrase “one by one.”
The how-question asks how I create a use case diagram for a person, with the person understood as acquiring a gym membership. “Here” can modify the acquisition.
The opening bird fragment is absorbed into the first switch command. The bird becomes an extent of the switch, and the top-right location attaches to that switch.
The imperative requests a grouped bar chart of average claim, with the breakdown by both policy type and region linked to how the chart is drawn.

Both placement commands are present, but the left-facing modifier is assigned to the tree, leaving the bear without its intended orientation.
The two add commands preserve the sequence, the heading name “Grandma's soup,” and the exact quoted text as the content of the paragraph.
